sources.entry: bit - Fast, lightweight, resource-efficient, compiled URL shortener. MIT Docker/Crystal

summary.one_liner: bit is a fast, lightweight, self-hosted URL shortener written in Crystal, distributed as a Docker image and deployable via Docker Compose or Dokku.
summary.what_it_does: bit shortens URLs and records click analytics: country, browser, OS and referer. It states it uses no cookies or persistent tracking beyond what a basic client request provides. Redirect responses include X-Forwarded-For and User-Agent headers, with caching disabled. Multiple users are supported through API key authentication, and keys are created, listed and deleted through a CLI. The README says the UA regexes and GeoLite2 database update automatically. Setup is configured through environment variables such as ENV, DATABASE_URL, APP_URL, ADMIN_NAME and ADMIN_API_KEY, and it uses SQLite as its database in the examples.
use_cases: track link clicks by country and browser
manage API keys for multiple users of a link shortener
deploy a short-link service on Dokku
run a lightweight redirect service in Docker
how_to_run: docker run --name bit -p 4000:4000 -e ENV="production" -e DATABASE_URL="sqlite3://./sqlite/data.db" -e APP_URL=" -e ADMIN_NAME="Admin" -e ADMIN_API_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32) sjdonado/bit
Dokku: create the app, set domains, configure storage and config:set variables as shown in the README, then add ports http:80:4000 and https:443:4000
notable: Very high throughput claimed: 21k req/sec, 6ms latency, about 32 MiB average memory in the README benchmark
Image size under 20 MiB with minimal dependencies
Privacy-minded analytics: no cookies or persistent tracking beyond the basic request
Ruby on Rails inspired structure, described as easy to extend
Listed under URL Shorteners on awesome-selfhosted
caveats: The README says new features are not planned; only bug fixes will continue
Example deployments use SQLite with a mounted storage directory, so the database is tied to a single host
Benchmark figures are the author's and come from a specific test setup
keywords: deploy url shortener on my server
